headline: Local IT Professional Informs Relatives That Thanksgiving Dinner Conflict Is Actually A 'Thucydides Trap'
body:
Vikram Sethi, a 34-year-old software architect, has officially reclassified his uncle’s insistence on talking politics during the main course as a high-stakes 'Thucydides Trap,' arguing that their inevitable clash for control of the TV remote is a fundamental structural tension between established and rising powers.

"I tried to explain to my Auntie that when she refuses to acknowledge my promotion at work while my cousin is currently doing a Master's abroad, she is essentially functioning as the declining Spartan hegemon," said Sethi, who spent three hours yesterday evening sketching a geopolitical map of the living room on a napkin. "The transition of power from the 'Older Generation' to the 'Millennial Cohort' is historically prone to conflict; I’m just trying to avoid a Peloponnesian-level event involving cold potato salad."

Sethi’s family members, who mostly just wanted to know if he was going to finish his broccoli, have largely remained unimpressed by his academic pivot. His uncle, 58-year-old Ramesh, reportedly responded to the historical analogy by noting that if Sethi didn't pass the plate of naan immediately, he would unilaterally impose trade sanctions on the dessert tray, effectively nullifying any diplomatic progress made since the appetizer round.
